name: Dragging Movements
explanation: Any feature that requires a dragging motion, like reordering a list by dragging items, or moving a slider handle, must also be operable through some other single-pointer method that doesn't require dragging, such as a long press followed by tapping a destination, or up/down arrow buttons next to a reorderable item. Dragging demands sustained, precise motor control that not everyone can perform reliably, so an alternative interaction path needs to exist. The exception is when dragging itself is essential to the function, which is uncommon.
whoItAffects: People with motor disabilities, tremors, or limited fine motor control often struggle to perform a sustained drag gesture, which requires holding a press, moving accurately, and maintaining contact throughout the entire motion; releasing early or drifting off-target can fail the action entirely partway through. Alternatives like tapping a target destination, or dedicated move-up/move-down buttons, break the same task into discrete, more forgiving steps that don't demand continuous precise motion.

codeExample.bad:
• Task 1
  • Task 2
  • Task 3
codeExample.good:
• Task 1
  • Task 2

howToTest: Find any feature on the page that requires a drag gesture: reordering list items, moving a slider, dragging a file onto a drop zone, adjusting a value with a draggable handle. For each one, check whether the same result can be achieved another way using a single pointer action that doesn't require sustained dragging, such as tapping arrow buttons to reorder, clicking directly on a slider track to jump to a value, or a file-picker button as an alternative to drag-and-drop upload. If dragging is the only way, and it isn't essential to the function, this fails.

check.question: A task management app lets users reorder their to-do list only by dragging items with the mouse or a touch gesture; there are no move-up/move-down buttons or any other alternative way to change the order. Does this pass SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements?
choices: Yes, because drag-and-drop reordering is an intuitive, widely used pattern
No, because there's no alternative single-pointer method to reorder items without dragging
Yes, because reordering isn't essential functionality
It depends only on whether the drag handles are large enough to grab
